title: Sharing Fair
learning_objectives: Learn that sharing can be fun

events.description: Your friend came over to play! You have 6 toys. How do you want to share?

choices.label: 3 toys each — split evenly!
choices.effect: You each get 3 toys! That feels really fair!

choices.label: Give your friend their favorite toy
choices.effect: Your friend is so happy you picked their favorite! What a kind thing to do!

events.description: You're both playing and your friend wants to try the toy you're using. What do you do?

choices.label: Take turns!
choices.effect: Taking turns means everyone gets a chance! Great idea!

choices.label: Trade for a different toy
choices.effect: You swapped toys and both found something fun! Nice trading!

events.description: It's almost time for your friend to go home. There's one toy left to play with together!

choices.label: Play with it together
choices.effect: You played together and had twice the fun!

choices.label: Let your friend have the last turn
choices.effect: Your friend loved the last turn! You're such a kind friend!

recap_template: You practiced sharing with a friend today! You learned that sharing and taking turns makes playtime more fun for everyone.
positive_framing_rules: Never say a sharing choice was selfish or wrong
Celebrate both equal sharing and generous choices
Frame all outcomes as positive for the friendship
ai_variation_allowed: Change the types of toys being shared
Describe the fun games they play together

title: How Does That Feel?

events.description: Your friend draws you a picture and gives it to you. How does that make you feel?

choices.label: Happy!
choices.effect: That's right! Getting a gift from a friend can make us feel happy and warm inside!

choices.label: Surprised!
choices.effect: Yes! Surprises can feel exciting and fun!

events.description: Oh no, you drop your ice cream on the ground. How might you feel?

choices.label: Sad
choices.effect: It's okay to feel sad when something doesn't go the way we hoped. Feelings pass!

choices.label: Frustrated
choices.effect: It's okay to feel frustrated! That happens to everyone sometimes.

events.description: Your teacher says you did a great job on your drawing! How does that feel?

choices.label: Proud!
choices.effect: Feeling proud means you know you tried your best! That's wonderful!

choices.label: Excited!
choices.effect: Getting praise can make us feel excited and eager to do more!

recap_template: You did a great job naming feelings today! Knowing how we feel helps us understand ourselves and be kind to others.
positive_framing_rules: Never say an emotion is wrong or bad
Validate all feelings as normal and okay
Use simple, warm language to describe emotions
ai_variation_allowed: Change the specific scenarios that trigger emotions
Describe how the body might feel with each emotion

title: Making Friends
learning_objectives: Learn what makes a good friend
Think about how words make others feel

events.description: A new kid is sitting alone at the playground. What do you do?

choices.label: Say hi and ask to play
choices.effect: You said hi! The new kid smiles and wants to play! Great job reaching out!

choices.label: Share your toy with them
choices.effect: You shared your toy! The new kid's face lights up! So kind!

events.description: Your new friend trips and falls down. What do you do?

choices.label: Help them up
choices.effect: You helped them up and asked if they were okay. That's what friends do!

choices.label: Get a teacher to help
choices.effect: You got a grown-up to help! That was smart and caring!

events.description: Your new friend wants to play a different game than you. What do you do?

choices.label: Try their game first
choices.effect: You tried something new and it was really fun! Being open to new things is great!

choices.label: Play both games, take turns
choices.effect: Great idea! You each got to play your favorite game! Everyone wins!

recap_template: You practiced being a kind friend today! You learned that saying hi, helping others, and being flexible makes friendships grow.
positive_framing_rules: Never present unkind options as choices
Celebrate every kind action the student takes
Frame all social situations as opportunities to connect
ai_variation_allowed: Add dialogue from the new friend
Describe the games they play together
